teaser: Maya's onboarding procedure vanishes into chat scrollback, until she learns to give reusable work a permanent home as an Artifact.

scene.title: Why is my procedure buried in chat scrollback?
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Day 3 – "Why is my procedure buried in chat scrollback?"

Maya drafted a 10-step client onboarding procedure with Claude. She copied it into an email, but halfway through writing the email she realized a step was wrong. She scrolled back through 30 chat turns to find the procedure again. Her manager asked for an updated version two days later — Maya had no idea which chat it was in.

Her colleague showed her Artifacts: Claude can render the procedure as a standalone document in a dedicated panel, separate from the chat. The team can open it, edit it, save it, and come back to it later. No more hunting through scrollback.

takeaways: An Artifact is standalone work (document, code, chart, diagram) rendered in a dedicated side panel, separate from the chat transcript.
Artifacts persist across sessions, can be edited in place, versioned, and shared via a stable link with view, comment or edit permissions.
Decision rule: if the team will come back to edit, reference or share it, make an Artifact; a one-off answer or quick lookup stays in chat.
Artifacts and Projects both solve 'don't repeat yourself': Artifacts hold reusable deliverables, Projects centralize reference material.
